title: Duty Exemption for Economic Zones and High-Tech Parks
summary: This thread covers the evolution of duty-free import privileges for developers and industrial units operating within designated Economic Zones and High-Tech Parks. It evolved from basic exemptions to comprehensive duty-free status for capital machinery, construction materials, and raw materials under bonded warehouse facilities.

evolution.legal_basis: Transitioned from Customs Act 1969 to Customs Act 2023.
evolution.scope: Expanded to include construction materials, capital machinery, and raw materials under bonded facilities.

timeline.change: Formalized duty-free status for Economic Zones and High-Tech Parks.
Updated legal basis to the Customs Act, 2023 for Economic Zone industrial units.

Customs Act 1969: Under Section 19(1) of this Act, the government, in consultation with the National Board of Revenue, grants duty and tax exemptions on imported goods used for the development of economic zones.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: This Act is cited as a legal basis, read in conjunction with the Customs Act, for providing tax exemptions on imported goods required for economic zone development.
Bangladesh Economic Zones Act 2010: This Act provides the regulatory framework under which developers are appointed and authorized to carry out development activities in designated economic zones.
Economic Zone Developer: Developers appointed under the Bangladesh Economic Zones Act are eligible for exemptions on import duties, regulatory duties, supplementary duties, and value-added tax for goods used in zone development, provided they are registered for value-added tax.
The developer must obtain certification from the Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority for the specific description, quantity, and details of the imported goods to qualify for these tax benefits.

Exemptions do not apply to goods not directly related to development or construction, such as office equipment, appliances, or vehicles, nor to locally available construction materials like cement and steel products.
National Board of Revenue: The government exercises its exemption powers under the relevant tax laws in consultation with this body.
Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority: This authority is responsible for reviewing, approving, and certifying the list of goods imported by developers to ensure they meet the criteria for tax exemption.
Customs Duty: These duties are exempted for goods imported by economic zone developers, subject to strict compliance with specified terms and conditions.
Regulatory Duty: This duty is waived for eligible goods imported by authorized economic zone developers for development purposes.
Supplementary Duty: Authorized developers are exempt from paying this duty on imported goods utilized in the development of economic zones.
Value Added Tax: Exemption from this tax is granted to economic zone developers for imported construction and development goods, conditional upon the developer holding a valid registration.

(১) শিল্প ইউনিটকে কমপক্ষে ১০ মিলিয়ন ইউএস ডলার বা সমপরিমাণ অর্থ বিনিয়োগ করিতে হইবে অথবা সংশ্লিষ্ট শিল্প ইউনিটে অন্যূন ৫০০ জনবল কর্মরত থাকিতে হইবে।
(২) আমদানিকৃত যানবাহনের শুল্ক নিরূপণ ও খালাসের সময় অর্থনৈতিক অঞ্চল কর্তৃপক্ষের অনুমোদন ও তৎসংক্রান্ত প্রত্যয়নপত্র শুল্ক কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট দাখিল করিতে হইবে।
(৩) অনূর্ধ্ব ২০০০ সিসি ইঞ্জিন ক্ষমতার একটি সেডান কার এবং একটি মাইক্রোবাস/পিকআপ ভ্যান/ডাবল কেবিন পিকআপ আমদানি করা যাইবে।
(৪) আমদানিকৃত যানবাহন ৫ (পাঁচ) বছরের মধ্যে হস্তান্তর বা বিক্রয় করা যাইবে নাঃ
তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, ৫ (পাঁচ) বছরের মধ্যে বিক্রয় বা হস্তান্তরের ক্ষেত্রে জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ডের ২৫ জুলাই, ২০০০ তারিখের স্থায়ী আদেশ (শুল্ক) No. 100/2000/shulka এর বিধান প্রযোজ্য হইবে।
(৫) অর্থনৈতিক অঞ্চলের কোন শিল্প ইউনিট এই প্রজ্ঞাপনের আওতায় কেবলমাত্র একবার যানবাহন আমদানি করিতে পারিবে।
(৬) এই প্রজ্ঞাপনের আওতাধীন আমদানিকৃত যানবাহনের নম্বর প্লেটের ক্রমিক নম্বরের পূর্বে "বেজা" শব্দটি লিখিতে হইবে।
(৭) এই প্রজ্ঞাপনের আওতাধীন আমদানিকৃত যানবাহন আমদানিকারক শিল্প ইউনিটের উৎপাদন ও সংশ্লিষ্ট কাজ ব্যতিরেকে অন্য কোন কাজে বা কোন বাণিজ্যিক উদ্দেশ্যে ব্যবহার করা যাইবে না।

Customs Act 1969: Section 19(1) of this Act empowers the Government to grant exemptions from customs duties, regulatory duties, value added tax, and supplementary duties in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(1) of this Act is read in conjunction with the Customs Act 1969 to facilitate the granting of duty and tax exemptions for industrial units in economic zones.
National Board of Revenue: The Government grants exemptions under this order after consulting with the National Board of Revenue.
The National Board of Revenue's established standing order regarding the transfer or sale of vehicles within a specified period remains applicable if the vehicles are transferred or sold prematurely.
Bangladesh Economic Zones Act 2010: This Act provides the legal framework for establishing economic zones and defining the entities authorized to operate industrial units therein.
Import Duty: Industrial units operating within designated economic zones are granted an exemption from import duty, regulatory duty, value added tax, and supplementary duty for imported vehicles, subject to specific compliance conditions.
Passenger Vehicle: Industrial units in economic zones are permitted to import one sedan car with an engine capacity not exceeding a specific limit and one microbus, pickup van, or double-cabin pickup.

Imported vehicles are subject to strict usage restrictions, requiring them to be used solely for production or related purposes, and they cannot be sold or transferred within a defined five-year period without following prescribed regulations.
All vehicles imported under this exemption must display specific identification markings on their number plates and are limited to a single import instance per industrial unit.

Economic Zone: Industrial units established within an economic zone are permitted to import raw materials or inputs for production under a bonded warehouse system.
Import Duty: Industrial units in economic zones may import production materials without paying applicable import duties under the bonded warehouse facility.
Supplementary Duty: Supplementary duty is exempt for industrial units operating within an economic zone when importing production inputs under the bonded warehouse system.
Value Added Tax: Industrial units in economic zones are allowed to import production-related materials without the payment of Value Added Tax under the bonded warehouse facility.
Bonded Warehouse Operation: The bonded warehouse facility is granted to industrial units in economic zones to facilitate the duty-free import of raw materials or inputs used for production.

Customs Act 1969: Section 19(1) of this Act empowers the government to grant exemptions from customs duties and other taxes for the import of capital machinery and construction materials by industrial units within a High-Tech Park.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(1) of this Act is read in conjunction with the Customs Act to facilitate tax exemptions for imports related to the establishment of High-Tech Parks.
High-Tech Park Authority Act 2010: This Act provides the legal framework under which industrial units in High-Tech Parks are established and authorizes the specific tax exemptions for imported machinery and construction materials.
High-Tech Park Industrial Units: Industrial units operating within a High-Tech Park are eligible for exemptions from import duties, regulatory duties, supplementary duties, and value added tax on machinery and construction materials, provided they are registered for value added tax.

The exemption is strictly limited to capital machinery and construction materials required for park development and construction; it excludes non-essential items such as office equipment, appliances, furniture, food, and beverages.
High-Tech Park Authority: The Authority is responsible for reviewing, approving, and certifying the list of imported goods, including their descriptions and quantities, to qualify for tax exemption benefits.
Import Duty Exemption: Exemptions are granted for capital machinery and construction materials imported by High-Tech Park units, subject to certification by the relevant Authority.
The exemption explicitly excludes locally available construction materials like steel rods, cement, prefabricated buildings, and iron sheets to promote local industry.

Supplementary Duty: The bonded system permits the deferment of supplementary duty for raw materials imported by industrial units established within high-tech parks.
Value Added Tax: Value added tax payments are not required at the time of import for raw materials brought into high-tech parks by industrial factories under the bonded arrangement.

Import Duty Exemption: Developers appointed under the High-Tech Park Authority Act are eligible for exemptions from import duties, regulatory duties, supplementary duties, and value added tax for goods used in high-tech park development. To qualify, developers must be registered for value added tax and obtain certification from the high-tech park authorities for the goods being imported.

The exemption does not apply to construction materials that are readily available in Bangladesh, such as steel rods, cement, and iron sheets. It also excludes items not directly related to park construction and development, including office equipment, air conditioners, refrigerators, passenger vehicles, and household goods.

Customs Act 1969: goods used for the development of high-tech parks
Import Duty Exemption: goods used in high-tech park development

Customs Act 1969: Section 19(1) of this Act empowers the Government to grant exemptions from customs duties and other related taxes in the public interest.
Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: Section 126(1) of this Act provides the legal authority for the Government to grant exemptions from Value Added Tax, Supplementary Duty, and Advance Tax.
Export Processing Zone: Investors operating within Export Processing Zones are granted exemptions from various import-related taxes and duties for specified goods.
Goods: A wide range of industrial and operational goods listed in the table, including machinery, safety equipment, office supplies, and power systems, are exempted from import duties, regulatory duties, value added tax, supplementary duty, and advance tax when imported by investors in Export Processing Zones.
H.S. Code: The exemption applies to the specific goods identified by the corresponding H.S. Codes listed in the schedule, with one category allowing exemptions regardless of the code.
Advance Tax: Investors in Export Processing Zones are explicitly exempted from paying Advance Tax on the import of the specified categories of industrial and operational goods.

Customs Act 2023: This Act serves as the primary legal authority under which the Government provides duty and tax exemptions to industrial units operating within economic zones.
Section 25(1) of this Act is cited as the enabling provision for granting these fiscal concessions.
Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: Section 126(1) of this Act provides the legal basis, in conjunction with the Customs Act 2023, for exempting industrial units in economic zones from certain value added taxes and supplementary duties.
Bangladesh Economic Zones Act 2010: This Act provides the regulatory framework for establishing economic zones and defines the operational context for industrial units eligible for duty and tax concessions.
Customs Duty: Industrial units in economic zones are granted an exemption from customs duty on construction materials and capital machinery to the extent that the duty rate exceeds one percent ad valorem.
Regulatory Duty: Industrial units in economic zones are exempted from the payment of all regulatory duties on qualified imported construction materials and capital machinery.
Supplementary Duty: The order grants an exemption from supplementary duty on the importation of eligible construction materials and capital machinery by industrial units in economic zones.
Value Added Tax: Industrial units must be registered for value added tax to qualify for the import duty and tax exemptions provided under this order.
Economic Zone Industrial Unit: Industrial units located within economic zones are eligible for duty and tax concessions on imported construction materials and capital machinery, provided they are registered for value added tax and obtain certification from the economic zone authority.

This exemption does not apply to locally available construction materials such as iron bars, cement, or prefabricated buildings, nor to consumer goods like office equipment, air conditioners, or food items.

Customs Act 2023: This act provides the enabling authority under Section 25 for the government to issue specific customs regulations and trade concessions.
Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: Section 126(1) of this act grants the government the power to issue regulations concerning tax exemptions and administrative procedures for imports.
Bank Guarantee: Industrial units without warehouse licenses must provide an unconditional and continuous bank guarantee equal to the total import duties, regulatory duties, value added tax, advance tax, and supplementary duties applicable to imported raw materials.
Integrated VAT Automated System: Purchase and sale contracts related to imported raw materials must be endorsed by the relevant lien bank within this system, or updated via the prescribed VAT registration form if the bank is not registered.
Industrial IRC Holder: This term refers to an entity that possesses a valid Industrial Registration Certificate issued by the Office of the Chief Controller of Imports and Exports.
VAT Compliant: This status denotes an entity registered under the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012 that fulfills all requirements regarding record-keeping, issuing tax invoices, and submitting periodic tax returns.
Commissioner of Customs, Excise and VAT: This authority is responsible for approving and countersigning the coefficients of production and waste (Input-Output Coefficient), and for inspecting raw materials and finished goods maintained by industrial units.
Manufacturer: Entities qualifying for these import benefits must be established manufacturers that are both industrial IRC holders and compliant with VAT laws.

Industrial IRC Holder: Office of the Chief Controller of Imports and Exports
